mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE values.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% may signal monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show negative returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows after FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high, it may indicate a overheating economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following strong GDP growth and high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) during an economic expansion indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following strong employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following rising industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 7% may indicate economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a significant drop in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following increases in housing starts and retail sales.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) during a late-cycle expansion may indicate upcoming economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show negative returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a GDP growth slowdown.
